newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSI says in iron ore talks with Hamersley.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSI says in iron ore talks with Hamersley.

text.p: AUSI Ltd said on Wednesday it was in talks with RTZ-CRA unit Hamersley Iron for the supply of 7.5 million tonnes of iron ore fines a year for its proposed iron ore pellet project in Western Australia.

The project would be based on iron ore supply from Hamersley's existing Paraburdoo mine southeast of Port Hedland, Patrick Patterson, managing director of AUSI Ltd, said in a speech scheduled to be delivered later on Wednesday to the Australia-Pacific Iron Ore and Steel Forum.
"AUSI is currently negotiating a bankable supply agreement with Hamersley for the 7.5 million tonnes per annum of fines," Patterson said.
All environmental approvals have been obtained for the project and AUSI was in the process of finalising negotiations to gain clear title to the site and its access corridors, he said.
Natural gas would be drawn from one or a number of gas projects on the North-West Shelf, he said.
The project would involve a capital cost of US$1.5 billion (A$1.9 billion), Patterson added.
Production would begin early in year 2000 at four million tonnes a year of direct reduced iron pellets, with full production to be reached by early 2001, he said.

Patterson said privately-held AUSI -- Australian United Steel Industry Ltd -- had obtained commitments for 25 percent of its output and letters of intent for quantities of DRI "well in excess of total plant production with a variety of customers throughout Asia".
"We are in the process of converting these letters of intent to bankable contracts and this activity will continue over the next six to nine months," he said.
Patterson said the project would be Australia's largest industrial project financed on a limited recourse basis.
"AUSI is well-advanced with several additional core equity participants and we are confident that this element will not hold back the project," he said.
Discussions with the Western Australian state government over state agreement for the project were well advanced, with approval expected during the second half of this year, he said.

"AUSI expects to be in a position to proceed with its capital-raising programme involving both debt and equity financing in Australia and internationally through to financial close in the first quarter of 1998," Patterson said.
The project is to be constructed on a 1,500 hectare site at Mt Anketel, between Karratha and Wickham on the northwest coast of Western Australia.
Patterson said the decision to focus on direct reduced iron was based on a belief that DRI was the most cost-effective solution to growing demands for electric arc furnace steelmaking feedstock.
Patterson was appointed managing director of AUSI last December following the entry of Norwegian construction group Kvaerner ASA as a major equity partner in AUSI Ltd.
He was formerly managing director of the Norweigan group's Melbourne-based subsidiary Kvaerner Energy Pty Ltd.
